newsitem.title: UK: Next tumbles after Oasis profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Next tumbles after Oasis profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Next Plc and other leading UK retailers dropped on Tuesday as Oasis Stores Plc rocked the sector with the second gloomy trading statement in as many days.
Next, which touched a record 757p on Monday -- up around 45 percent from its level in early January -- fell 22p to 708p while Great Universal Stores Plc was down 13p to 632p by 1358 GMT.
Hard on the heels of a warning of a sales shortfall from John David Sport on Monday, Oasis warned its first half profits for the current year would be lower than for the same period last year.
Shares in Oasis plummeted 73p to 267-1/2p in volume of 223,000 shares.
Analysts said highly rated stores stocks were probably due a correction, particularly with the UK budget looming at the beginning of July.
"Next has been partly affected by the Oasis warning and I think investors have been looking for an excuse to take profits in the stock," said a stores analyst at a leading UK securities house.
Analysts said the forthcoming budget could have more influence on the sector than adverse news on interest rates following the Bank of England's monetary policy meeting on Friday.
"Investors believe any fiscal tightening exercised by this government in the budget could affect consumer spending in the sector," he added.
Dealers noted the fall of shares in John David Sport and JJB Sports have been exacerbated by the current quarter profit warning from Nike Inc at the end of last week.
Shares in John David Sport fell 22p to 249p, while JJB Sports dropped 19-1/2p to 473p.
